Subject: Light Up a Life 2026 — draft for Moira to review

Hilary asked the other day whether we are doing the tree again this year. We are, Hilary, and it will be lovely to welcome you and your sister. Your message about your mum reminded me that it was time to put the details here for everyone.

Our Light Up a Life tree will be in the bookshop window again this November, with room for the names of people we miss.

It is seven years this month since my husband Ray died at the hospice. The first year I hung his tag on the tree, I could hardly write it. Now I write it at the counter in the shop, with the same pen. I still have to stop for a moment, but I am glad to be writing his name among all the others. There is something comforting about seeing them together, even when you don't know the people whose names you are reading.

And that is what the tree is for. You do not have to have had someone cared for by the hospice. It is for anyone grieving, whether your loss is very recent or you have been living with it for years. You are welcome to remember someone here.

Memory tags will be available in the shop from Monday 16 November, with a suggested donation of £3. There will be envelopes on the counter if you would rather take yours home and write it there. Some things are easier at your own kitchen table, and some are easier with a bit of company. Either is quite all right.

We will switch on the lights on Saturday 28 November at 4pm. The children from Gildencroft Primary are coming back to sing a few carols, and Doreen is making mince pies again. Judging by last year, I wouldn't leave it too late for one of those.

Every name on the tags will be read aloud at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December, at 3pm in the day centre. You do not need to attend the service for your loved one's name to be read.

Please also know that you can simply come and stand by the tree. You needn't buy a book, write a tag or explain why you have come. If you would like a quiet look at the names and the lights, there is a place for you too.

Thank you to everyone who helped make last year's tree what it was: those who wrote the 412 tags, those who came to listen and sing, and those who stood beside someone who needed a little company. I remember the kindness of that evening as much as anything.

We look forward to remembering with you again.

Jean
